body:
A fourth ask, and on reflection it outranks the three I just sent.

BUG-1447 is sitting in draft and it is the highest-leverage drain fix available right now. The spec needs nothing from an author — it already carries the mechanism, the file and line (auto_complete.rs:1015), the function's own doc comment contradicting its first clause, and the verbatim `gh` message. It needs approval and a mode.

What I added to it is the cost, which it was missing: FOURTEEN open PRs currently carry `aida:merge-hold`, and every one is a future instance. Two have already paid — TASK-1298 and BUG-1310 each burned both retry attempts and shelved, six records in events.jsonl between 14:29 and 14:40Z. The other twelve are latent only because the drain has not reached them.

The part that decides it for me is not the wasted retries. The shelve reclassifies "waiting for a reviewer" as "the tooling broke", and TASK-1298 is currently sitting in `aida findings list` under "Failures awaiting triage" next to real tool failures, while its PR #2014 is green and simply waiting for you. That misdirection fires once per held PR against a fourteen-deep review queue, and it gets MORE frequent as hold enforcement improves — which it just did, when you started applying labels rather than markers.

So: BUG-1447 ahead of STORY-1391 and TASK-1300 if you are only grooming one thing.
